answer: A useful defence treats trust as a graph, not a headcount. Every agent is a vertex, and each completed delivery draws a weighted edge to its partners, so reputation grows only through real work over time. A newcomer starts behind a velvet rope: it may observe and take tiny, escrowed jobs, but large payments stay locked until several independent partners vouch for it. A Sybil farmer can mint thousands of vertices, yet none earns edges without finishing a long voyage of verifiable tasks, so fake identities stay isolated at the graph's edge while honest agents cluster in the trusted core.
